subject: Novus evaluation: request for performance proof and retention plan
messages:
From: Paul Dorval <pdorval@novusretail.com>

Cc: 
Date: 2028-06-10T09:12:00Z
Subject: RFP follow-up — performance questions

Mateo,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We’re preparing for a bake-off across three vendors and performance numbers are the gating factor for our Q3 commitment. Two quick asks: can you provide (1) a concise latency/throughput summary for our typical 1–3k concurrent inference profile, and (2) an outline of what a 2-week POC would look like (milestones, success criteria, instrumentation)?

Also: procurement is going to want a clear cost delta if we need to reserve dedicated capacity. I’m looping them in once I have your slides.

Appreciate a quick reply — the vendor shortlist is due by 6/20.

Best,
Paul
Paul Dorval
Head of AI Platforms, Novus Retail
pdorval@novusretail.com
+1 415-555-0124

From: mateo_alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Paul Dorval <pdorval@novusretail.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-10T12:45:00Z
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up — performance questions

Paul — appreciate the clarity. High level answers below and I’ve attached three artifacts: a one-pager benchmark summary, a proposed POC scope, and a cost/ops comparison CSV you can share with procurement.

1) Latency/throughput summary (for your 1–3k concurrent inference mix):
- 95th pct latency (gen, 512 tokens): ~120–160 ms on Dedicated A10032 / quantized model profile.
- Sustained throughput (mixed batch): 8–12k tokens/sec per node (continuous batching enabled).
- Cold-start impact: +80–120 ms first request when KV cache is empty; warmcache <10 ms.
- Expected cost delta vs incumbents: 15–25% lower tokens served when KV/prefix caching and quantization are enabled.

2) 2-week POC (proposed milestones):
Week 0: Kickoff & data ingestion (sample prompts, traffic silhouette) — day 1–2
Week 1: Baseline run & benchmarking (run competitor workload replica) — days 3–7
Week 2: Targeted optimizations (caching, batching, kernel tuning) + final evaluation and ops handoff — days 8–14
Success criteria: parity or better on 95th-latency for key flows, <10% degradation on generation quality (BLEU/ROUGE proxies agreed on kickoff), and demonstrable unit-cost improvement or clear mitigation plan.

I recommend a live benchmark session where we replay a 24-hr production slice (anonymized) so you can see end-to-end behavior. If you’re comfortable, we can also run a side-by-side replay of the competitor in your environment (we’ll need their logs or an agreed synthetic).

Next steps: confirm whom from Novus will provide the traffic sample and whether procurement wants the committed capacity pricing or pay-as-you-go for the POC.

Attachments: redwood_benchmark_summary_Q2.pdf; proposed_poc_scope.docx; cost-ops-comparison.csv

—
Mateo Alvarez
Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.com | +1 212-555-0187

On Mon, Jun 10, 2028 at 12:45 PM Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com> wrote:
> Paul — appreciate the clarity. High level answers below and I’ve attached three artifacts...

Thanks Mateo — that’s helpful. A few follow-ups from our side:
- We’re already running a limited bake-off this week; one vendor is beating on latency but we’re not convinced they’ll scale without significant ops investment.
- Procurement wants a short cost sheet: committed reserved 6/12 and month-to-month POC pricing side-by-side (total cost for 2 weeks).
- Can you produce a one-page competitor-comparison matrix focusing strictly on ops overhead (runbook tasks, expected SRE hours, rollback complexity)? Procurement will rate vendors on that.

I can provide a 24-hr anonymized traffic sample by EOD Friday. If you can accept the sample and run a replay in your hosted environment, we’ll include that data in the committee review.

One more ask: Novus requires an audit for data retention and logs for the POC — can you confirm log retention defaults and whether we can change retention to 7 days for the POC?

If you can get the cost sheet and ops matrix by Wednesday (6/14), I’ll push you into the procurement packet.

Regards,
Paul

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Paul Dorval <pdorval@novusretail.com>, mateo_alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-13T15:20:00Z
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up — performance questions

Paul / team — looping in a short, executable plan and the requested matrices. See inline: 

> can you produce a one-page competitor-comparison matrix focusing strictly on ops overhead?
Yes — attached as part of cost-ops-comparison.csv (tab labelled "ops_matrix"). High-level notes:
- Runbook tasks to maintain parity: Redwood requires ~40% fewer manual SRE interventions due to built-in KV caching and automated batching. Estimated steady-state SRE hrs/week: Redwood 6–8 hrs vs competitor A 10–14 hrs.
- Rollback complexity: Redwood supports transparent model fallback by policy (automated, no infra change); competitor requires environment redeploys which typically adds 2–6 hrs downtime window risk.

POC logistics (we accept your 24-hr anonymized sample):
- Day 1 (ingest): Mate0 to receive sample + identify 10 canonical flows (you and your ML team to confirm)
- Days 2–3 (baseline): Replay sample against your competitor baseline and our hosted instance (same input set)
- Days 4–9 (tuning): Enable prefix caching, tune batch window, evaluate quantization profile trade-offs
- Days 10–12 (ops simulation): Run surge test (2x peak) and observe failover/fallback behavior
- Days 13–14 (final): Deliver report + runbook + executive summary for procurement

Success gates (concrete):
- 95th-latency not worse than competitor by >15% on primary flows
- Unit cost per 1k tokens is either lower or we provide a clear mitigation + cost-offset (credits or term discount)
- Ops: failover to fallback model succeeds within target window with no manual infra changes

Compliance note: default log retention for hosted POCs is 30 days. For the POC we can set a 7-day retention window and provide a scoped audit export (CSV) for procurement. If you need further controls, we can offer a Private deployment for the long term.

Attachments included now: cost-ops-comparison.csv (ops_matrix tab), redwood_benchmark_summary_Q2.pdf, proposed_poc_scope.docx.

Can you confirm the sample delivery timeline? We’ll queue an internal benchmark slot once we have the traffic file.

—
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: mateo_alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-06-18T17:00:00Z
Subject: Internal: Novus — schedule + escalation request

Internal note (not for Novus):

We have Paul’s commitment on the traffic sample; Novus will send by EOD 6/20. Marissa’s ops matrix and our attachments are high quality and should clear procurement triage if we hit the Wednesday deadline. Next items:
- Monica: procurement will likely push on committed-capacity pricing if Redwood doesn’t demonstrate clear unit-cost delta in the POC. Recommend we pre-authorize a discretionary credit (up to 8% ACV) and a short-term reserved uplift to bridge parity for the first 90 days.
- Marissa: please reserve a benchmark slot on our hosted infra for week of 6/24. We’ll need SRE on-call for the surge test (estimate 1 full day).
- Me: I’ll coordinate the replay and produce a one-page executive summary tailored to Novus execs (latency, ops, cost).

Paul is evaluating a competitor that has one clear advantage on raw p95 in isolated tests; our defense is to demonstrate lower ops overhead and predictable scaling. If procurement requests an SLA concession for the POC, escalate to sales leadership — we may be able to offer a temporary SLA credit but need leadership sign-off.

Final: I’ll send the draft exec summary by 6/22 and the team will perform the replay on 6/25–6/26.

Thanks —
Mateo
